simple: Should each region and town decide its own matters, without waiting for the national government?

example.agree: A town decides on its own when buses run and how wide sidewalks are.
example.disagree: The national government sets the same transport rules for every town.

simple: Should laws be the same across the whole country, even if some region wants something else?

example.agree: The age to get a driver's license is the same in every region.
example.disagree: Each region chooses its own minimum driving age.

simple: Should rules about local matters be made by the town or region itself?

example.agree: The town council decides where bars can stay open late.
example.disagree: A national law sets bar hours for every town.

simple: Should every school in the country teach the same content, instead of each region choosing?

example.agree: A student who moves to another region picks up the lessons exactly where they left off.
example.disagree: Each region adds its own local history and culture to the school program.

simple: Should each state or province be able to write its own main rulebook, its own way, without the national government deciding for it?

example.agree: A province decides in its own constitution that school starts later, and the national government can't change that.
example.disagree: The main rules are the same across the country, so someone who moves to another region keeps exactly the same rights.

simple: Is it better to have one police force for the whole country than a separate one in each region?

example.agree: A single police force follows a suspect from one region to another without asking for help.
example.disagree: Each region runs its own police and decides how to handle its own problems.

simple: Should most tax money stay in the town or region where it was paid?

example.agree: Taxes paid in your town fix the streets of your own town.
example.disagree: The national government pools taxes and sends more money to poorer regions.

simple: Should public hospitals across the country follow the same rules, under one central command?

example.agree: During an epidemic, one agency sets the rules for every hospital.
example.disagree: Each region runs its hospitals in the way that works best for it.

simple: If most people in a region vote to leave the country, should it be able to become a new country?

example.agree: A region holds a vote, most choose to leave, and it becomes an independent country.
example.disagree: Even after the vote, the region stays part of the country.

simple: Should regional taxes follow national rules so regions don't fight each other over them?

example.agree: Every region charges similar taxes, so none lures companies away from another.
example.disagree: A region lowers its taxes to attract factories that were in another region.

simple: Should Indigenous and traditional peoples be able to live by their own rules on their lands?

example.agree: A village settles its internal disputes using its own customs.
example.disagree: The same laws as the rest of the country apply inside the village.

simple: Should work rules, like vacation and working hours, be the same in every region?

example.agree: A worker has the same rights anywhere in the country.
example.disagree: Each region adjusts work rules to fit its local economy.

simple: Should a town be able to make its own laws, even if they differ from national laws?

example.agree: A town bans plastic bags, even though the rest of the country allows them.
example.disagree: Towns can only follow and apply the laws made at the national level.

simple: When a regional leader and the national leader disagree, should the national leader have the final say?

example.agree: The national leader orders schools to reopen, and the region has to comply.
example.disagree: The regional leader keeps the region's schools closed, even though the national leader disagrees.

simple: Should the country be like a team of regions, each with lots of power to decide on its own?

example.agree: Each region has its own strong parliament and decides almost everything about itself.
example.disagree: The national government decides most things, and regions handle only the details.

simple: Should the national government be able to cancel regional and local laws that hurt the country?

example.agree: A town passes a law that blocks a national highway, and the national government cancels it.
example.disagree: The town's law stands, because the people who live there chose it.

simple: Should regions with a strong culture of their own get more power to decide their own matters?

example.agree: A region with its own language and traditions runs its own schools and public TV.
example.disagree: Every region has the same power, no matter how different its culture is.

simple: Should a region be forbidden from leaving the country, even if most people there want to?

example.agree: A region votes to leave, but the country doesn't accept it, and it stays part of the country.
example.disagree: If most of the region wants to leave, the country lets it become independent.

simple: Should public schools be run by local governments rather than the national government?

example.agree: The town picks school principals and sets the school calendar.
example.disagree: The national government runs the schools so they all work the same way.

simple: Should regional and local leaders carry out what the national government decides, even on local matters?

example.agree: The national government sets the vaccination plan, and mayors just put it into action.
example.disagree: Each mayor decides how and when to vaccinate in their town.

simple: Should we keep having free elections, even when people choose bad governments?

example.agree: A bad government gets elected, and the fix is to wait for the next election to replace it.
example.disagree: When an elected government does great harm, elections are suspended to change course.

simple: In a very serious crisis, should a strong leader be able to rule without the legislature?

example.agree: In a disaster, the leader decides everything alone to act faster.
example.disagree: Even in a crisis, every major measure has to go through the legislature.

simple: Should people who oppose the government be able to criticize it in public, whatever the government?

example.agree: An opposition party runs TV ads saying the government is wrong.
example.disagree: Criticism that undermines the government at a difficult time is banned.

simple: Is it better for a small group of leaders to decide than to split power among several institutions?

example.agree: A council of five people decides quickly, without going through a legislature or courts.
example.disagree: A decision has to be approved by the legislature and can be reviewed by the courts.

simple: If the government makes a decision, should judges who weren't elected be able to cancel it?

example.agree: The government creates a rule that judges find goes against the constitution, and they cancel it.
example.disagree: The elected government makes a decision, and it stands even if some judges disagree.

simple: Should a good leader be able to be re-elected as many times as they want?

example.agree: A well-liked president runs for a fourth term in a row and wins.
example.disagree: After two terms, the president has to step down, even if popular.

simple: Should every adult be able to vote in secret, even people who don't follow politics?

example.agree: Someone who never reads the news votes, and their vote counts the same as anyone's.
example.disagree: Only people who pass a simple test about how the country works get to vote.

simple: Should a leader who does a good job be able to stay in power without facing elections?

example.agree: A leader who improved the economy keeps governing without new elections.
example.disagree: Even when doing well, the leader has to win a new election every few years.

simple: Should the people be able to strike down a law by voting directly, without the legislature?

example.agree: People gather signatures, hold a vote, and cancel a law they dislike.
example.disagree: Only the legislature can change or cancel laws that have already passed.

simple: Should leaders be chosen by skill, tradition, or inheritance, rather than by vote?

example.agree: A king passes the throne to his child, who was trained all their life to rule.
example.disagree: Any citizen can run for office, and the people choose by voting.

simple: Should voters be able to remove a bad politician before their term ends?

example.agree: A mayor breaks promises, residents hold a vote, and the mayor loses the job.
example.disagree: The mayor stays until the end of the term, and voters judge them at the next election.

simple: Would you accept a government without free elections if it made the country grow faster?

example.agree: A government with no opposition builds roads and factories fast, and the country gets richer.
example.disagree: The country grows more slowly, but people keep choosing who governs.

simple: Is it better for different parties to take turns in government than for one group to rule for decades?

example.agree: After a few years, another party wins the election and takes over.
example.disagree: The same party governs for 30 years and can carry out long-term plans.

simple: Should experts chosen for their knowledge govern, even without winning elections?

example.agree: A group of economists and engineers runs the country based on research.
example.disagree: Whoever governs is elected, and can bring in experts to help.

simple: Should those who govern need the approval of the people affected by their decisions?

example.agree: Before building a dam, the government consults the people who live in the area.
example.disagree: The government decides what's best for the country, even if residents object.

simple: Should only some people have the right to vote, rather than every adult?

example.agree: Only people with a certain level of education, or who pass a test, can vote.
example.disagree: Every adult votes, no matter how much schooling they have.

simple: Would it be better if residents decided everything in open meetings, without politicians?

example.agree: The neighborhood meets in the square and votes on how to spend public money.
example.disagree: Residents elect representatives, who decide on their behalf.

simple: Is governing efficiently more important than leaving room for the opposition?

example.agree: The government passes its laws quickly, without long debates with the opposition.
example.disagree: Laws take longer because the opposition gets time to debate and propose changes.

simple: Should even a government elected by a huge majority respect all of the opposition's rights?

example.agree: A government with 80% of the vote still lets the opposition speak, protest, and run.
example.disagree: With such a big win, the government can limit those who get in the way of its plans.

simple: Is a stable government without free elections better than a democracy full of crises?

example.agree: The same government stays for decades, without free elections, and the country is calm.
example.disagree: The country changes government often and goes through crises, but people keep voting.

simple: Should police carry out tough operations in areas controlled by organized crime?

example.agree: Police move in with force to take back a neighborhood controlled by criminals.
example.disagree: The government invests in investigations and services there, avoiding armed clashes.

simple: Should adults who use cannabis stop being treated as criminals?

example.agree: An adult smokes cannabis at home and can't be arrested for it.
example.disagree: Anyone caught using cannabis can be punished by law.

simple: Should the government be able to read phone and online messages to fight crime?

example.agree: Police monitor messages and uncover a robbery before it happens.
example.disagree: Your messages are private, and police can see them only with a judge's order in a specific case.

simple: Should people be free to say even things that offend others?

example.agree: Someone tells an offensive joke, gets criticized, but isn't punished by law.
example.disagree: Someone who says something very offensive in public can be fined.

simple: Should there be more street cameras that recognize who you are by your face, to help catch criminals?

example.agree: A camera spots someone wanted for robbery on the street, and the police find them the same day.
example.disagree: You go to a protest or a doctor's appointment and would rather no system recorded that you were there.

simple: Should things adults choose to do, like using drugs or gambling, stop being crimes?

example.agree: An adult gambles at a casino or uses drugs, and the police don't step in.
example.disagree: The law bans these activities to protect people and their families.

simple: Should the state be able to shut down political parties that threaten public order?

example.agree: A party that encourages violence is banned from running in elections.
example.disagree: Every party can exist; voters decide whether it wins or loses.

simple: Should all drugs, even the strongest, be legal for adults?

example.agree: Cocaine is sold in regulated shops, with labels and taxes, like alcohol.
example.disagree: Hard drugs stay banned, and dealers can go to prison.

simple: Should it be very hard for an ordinary person to get a gun?

example.agree: Getting a gun requires a strong reason, tests, and months of waiting.
example.disagree: Any adult without a criminal record can buy a gun easily.

simple: Should adults be allowed to keep a gun at home to defend themselves?

example.agree: A family keeps a gun at home to protect itself from intruders.
example.disagree: Only the police carry guns, and families rely on them for protection.

simple: In a serious situation, should the government be able to ban people from going out at night?

example.agree: During a wave of violence, no one can be on the street after 10 p.m.
example.disagree: Even in a crisis, each person decides when to leave home.

simple: Should someone with an incurable illness be able to ask for medical help to die?

example.agree: A terminally ill patient in great pain asks a doctor for help to die, and gets it.
example.disagree: Doctors treat the pain until the end, but can't help the patient die.

simple: Should getting vaccinated be mandatory, even for people who don't want to?

example.agree: A child can only enroll in school with up-to-date vaccinations.
example.disagree: Each family decides whether to vaccinate, even if most people do.

simple: If it's not certain someone is guilty, should they go free, even though they might be?

example.agree: There isn't enough evidence, so the suspect goes free, even though many think they did it.
example.disagree: With strong suspicion, the accused stays locked up so as not to risk everyone's safety.

simple: Should people who commit very serious crimes, like rape and murder, face the death penalty?

example.agree: A convicted murderer is sentenced to death.
example.disagree: The harshest punishment is prison, even for the worst crimes.

simple: Should what adults do in private, with everyone's consent, be outside criminal law?

example.agree: Two adults live however they like at home, and the state stays out of it.
example.disagree: Some private conduct stays banned to protect society's morals.

simple: Should the government be able to take down social media accounts that spread lies?

example.agree: An account spreading false rumors about vaccines is taken down.
example.disagree: The account stays up, and people decide whom to believe.

simple: Should the government be barred from seeing what you buy with a card or phone?

example.agree: Your card purchases stay between you and your bank, with no government access.
example.disagree: The government tracks payments to catch tax evasion and money laundering.

simple: Should terrorism suspects be held without trial until the danger has passed?

example.agree: Someone suspected of planning an attack is held for months, without trial, for safety.
example.disagree: Even a terrorism suspect has the right to a prompt trial.

simple: Should no one be forced to unlock their phone for the police?

example.agree: Police ask for your phone, you refuse to give the passcode, and you aren't punished.
example.disagree: If the police have an order, you have to unlock your phone.

simple: Should people who move to a country learn the language and live the local way?

example.agree: An immigrant takes language classes and starts celebrating the country's holidays.
example.disagree: An immigrant keeps their language and customs, and the country adapts to them too.

simple: Is it good for people in the same country to use several languages in daily life, not just the official one?

example.agree: Signs, schools, and public services also work in the languages people in the city speak.
example.disagree: Everything runs in the official language, and newcomers learn it so they can take part.

simple: Should the country close its doors to immigrants to keep its culture as it is?

example.agree: The country stops accepting new immigrants so its traditions don't change.
example.disagree: The country keeps welcoming immigrants, and its culture changes over time.

simple: Should immigrants be able to keep their customs, even if they're very different from local ones?

example.agree: An immigrant family keeps wearing traditional clothes and celebrating its own holidays.
example.disagree: The family is expected to set aside customs that clash with the country's.

simple: Should the country turn away immigrants who refuse to respect local customs?

example.agree: A visa is denied because the person says they won't follow the country's social norms.
example.disagree: The country admits the person and only requires that they obey the law.

simple: Should immigrants be able to live well here without giving up their customs?

example.agree: An immigrant gets a job and respect while keeping their religion and way of dressing.
example.disagree: To do well, an immigrant has to adapt to the country's way of life.

simple: Is keeping the country's traditions more important than making room for foreign customs?

example.agree: The city keeps only the country's traditional festivals on its official calendar.
example.disagree: The city adds festivals brought by immigrants to its calendar.

simple: Should the country encourage people of different languages and cultures to live together?

example.agree: The government supports festivals and schools that bring different cultures together.
example.disagree: The government focuses on one shared language and culture for everyone.

simple: Should the country prefer immigrants from cultures similar to its own?

example.agree: People from countries with a similar language and customs get visas faster.
example.disagree: All immigrants are assessed the same way, whatever their culture of origin.

simple: Should customs brought by immigrants become part of the country's identity?

example.agree: A dish brought by immigrants becomes a national favorite and a source of pride.
example.disagree: The country's identity stays tied to the traditions of those who already lived there.

simple: Should people who immigrate be required to adapt to local customs?

example.agree: To stay in the country, an immigrant has to take courses on local culture and norms.
example.disagree: An immigrant only has to obey the law; adapting to customs is their choice.

simple: Should your country keep taking in people fleeing serious crises in other countries?

example.agree: Families escaping hunger and violence get shelter and papers to work.
example.disagree: The country limits entry to deal first with the problems of people already living there.

simple: Should speaking the country's language well be one of the main requirements to immigrate?

example.agree: To get a visa, the person has to pass a test in the local language.
example.disagree: The person can arrive without speaking the language and learn it later.

simple: Should immigrants be seen as individuals, not judged by their home country's reputation?

example.agree: An immigrant is judged only by what they do, not by what people say about their country.
example.disagree: It's reasonable to consider customs common in a newcomer's country of origin.

simple: Do neighborhoods where immigrants live apart, only among themselves, cause problems for the country?

example.agree: In one neighborhood almost no one speaks the local language, making it hard to connect with the rest of the city.
example.disagree: Immigrants living near each other is natural and helps newcomers settle in.

simple: Should children of immigrants also be able to study in their parents' language?

example.agree: A child learns math in the local language and also in the family's language.
example.disagree: In public school, every class is taught only in the country's language.

simple: Should the country limit immigration so its main culture doesn't change?

example.agree: The country sets a yearly cap on immigrants to preserve its customs.
example.disagree: The country takes in whoever wants to come, even if the culture changes as a result.

simple: Should any peaceful person be able to come and live in the country?

example.agree: Someone from another continent arrives, shows a clean record, and can stay.
example.disagree: To live in the country you need a visa, and the country decides how many it accepts.

simple: Should immigrants who reject local customs lose the right to stay in the country?

example.agree: An immigrant who refuses to follow basic social norms loses their residence permit.
example.disagree: As long as they obey the law, the immigrant stays, even without following local customs.

simple: Do you feel more like a citizen of the world than of one particular country?

example.agree: You care as much about a problem across the world as one in your own country.
example.disagree: You feel a special bond with your country, its history, and its people.

simple: Should a country have strong armed forces to be respected by others?

example.agree: The country invests in modern planes and ships, and neighbors think twice before provoking it.
example.disagree: The country keeps a small military and earns respect through diplomacy and trade.

simple: Before any attack, should the country try every possible talk and negotiation?

example.agree: Even after a provocation, the country spends months negotiating before considering force.
example.disagree: If the threat is clear, the country acts right away, without waiting for long talks.

simple: If an enemy country seems to be getting ready to attack, can your country attack first?

example.agree: Satellite images show missiles being moved to the border, and the country destroys them before they are launched.
example.disagree: Even with signs of a threat, the country waits and only responds if it is actually attacked, because the signs could be wrong.

simple: Would you rather avoid a war even when it could benefit your country?

example.agree: The country could gain territory in a war, but chooses peace.
example.disagree: If war secures important gains, the country is willing to fight.

simple: Should the country put military spending first, even when other areas are short of money?

example.agree: The government buys new tanks, even with hospitals asking for more funding.
example.disagree: Money goes first to health and schools, and the military gets what's left.

simple: Should the country make deals with rivals, even if it has to give some things up?

example.agree: To end a border dispute, the country agrees to share an area with its neighbor.
example.disagree: The country gives up nothing, even if the dispute drags on for years.

simple: Should your country have nuclear weapons?

example.agree: With nuclear weapons, no country dares to attack yours.
example.disagree: Your country goes without them and pushes for no one in the world to have them.

simple: Should the country spend less on the military?

example.agree: Money saved on the military goes to schools and hospitals.
example.disagree: The country keeps military spending up so it's ready if threatened.

simple: Should every young person have to serve in the military so the country is ready for war?

example.agree: At 18, everyone spends a year training in the military.
example.disagree: Only people who want to join the military serve, as a career.

simple: Is making deals to reduce weapons more important than growing the country's arsenal?

example.agree: Two rival countries sign a deal and destroy half their missiles.
example.disagree: The country keeps buying weapons because it doesn't trust rivals to keep their word.

simple: Should the country make its own weapons instead of buying them abroad?

example.agree: The country builds its own fighter jets, even though it costs more.
example.disagree: The country buys ready-made jets from abroad, cheaper and faster to get.

simple: Does no political or ideological cause justify starting a war?

example.agree: Even to spread a system it thinks is better, the country attacks no one.
example.disagree: Some causes, like freeing an oppressed people, can justify starting a war.

simple: Should the government be allowed to spy on other countries?

example.agree: Spies uncover a rival country's plans before it acts.
example.disagree: The country spies on no one and relies on open agreements.

simple: Should your country back international courts that try war crimes, even when an ally is on trial?

example.agree: A general from a friendly country is put on international trial, and your country supports it.
example.disagree: Your country shields its allies and prefers that each nation try its own people.

simple: Should your country build weapons that choose and attack targets on their own, without a person deciding?

example.agree: Smart drones guard the border and react faster than any soldier.
example.disagree: Every decision to attack stays with a person, never a machine.

simple: Should your country talk even with hostile governments before threatening them militarily?

example.agree: Even with a hostile government, the country sends diplomats to negotiate first.
example.disagree: With hostile governments, the country shows strength right away, without talks.

simple: Should your country be ready to start a war if it secures things the country truly needs?

example.agree: A neighbor threatens to cut off a vital river, and the country is willing to attack.
example.disagree: The country fights only if attacked, and never starts a war.

simple: Should your country get rid of its armed forces?

example.agree: The country closes its military and spends the money on schools, as some small countries have done.
example.disagree: The country keeps an army to defend itself if attacked.

simple: Should the country warn that it would answer an attack with overwhelming force, so no one dares attack?

example.agree: The government makes clear any attack will meet a massive response, and rivals back off.
example.disagree: The country avoids threats, because they can raise tensions and lead to war.

simple: Should the United Nations try to resolve conflicts before any military action?

example.agree: Before a war, UN representatives bring both sides together to negotiate.
example.disagree: Each country decides on its own when to act, without waiting for the UN.

simple: Should a country never try to change another country's government?

example.agree: A country disagrees with its neighbor's government but leaves it to the people there.
example.disagree: A country backs a neighbor's opposition to topple a cruel government.

simple: Should your country pressure other countries when its national interest is at stake?

example.agree: Your country threatens to end a deal unless a neighbor allows sales of one of its products.
example.disagree: Your country respects other countries' decisions, even when it loses out.

simple: Should your country stay out of agreements that could force it to fight when a friendly country goes to war?

example.agree: A friendly country goes to war on the other side of the world, and your country doesn't have to send soldiers.
example.disagree: Your country belongs to a defense group, so if anyone attacks it, several countries come to help.

simple: Should foreign policy aim to increase your country's influence over its neighbors?

example.agree: Your country funds projects in neighboring countries to gain sway in regional decisions.
example.disagree: Your country treats its neighbors as equals, without trying to lead them.

simple: Should your country not send soldiers abroad, not even to help keep the peace?

example.agree: Other countries ask for troops to calm a conflict, and your country sends only humanitarian aid.
example.disagree: Your country sends soldiers on a UN peacekeeping mission on another continent.

simple: Should your country use diplomatic pressure to defend its interests abroad?

example.agree: Your country's diplomats negotiate hard to protect its companies abroad.
example.disagree: Your country avoids pressuring other governments, even when something harms it.

simple: Even if a neighbor is killing part of its own people, should your country stay out militarily?

example.agree: A massacre happens next door, and your country helps refugees but sends no troops.
example.disagree: Your country sends soldiers to stop the massacre.

simple: Should your country be able to impose economic penalties on countries that threaten its interests?

example.agree: A country harms yours, and your country stops buying its products.
example.disagree: Your country settles disputes by talking, without economic penalties.

simple: Should disputes between countries be settled by international organizations, not by the strongest countries?

example.agree: A border dispute goes to an international court, which decides who is right.
example.disagree: The most powerful countries meet and decide how to resolve the conflict.

simple: Should your country be the political leader of its region?

example.agree: Neighbors follow your country's position on the region's big decisions.
example.disagree: Each country in the region decides for itself, without a regional leader.

simple: Should your country avoid blocs that require it to always side with another power?

example.agree: Your country stays out of an alliance so it can deal with all sides.
example.disagree: Your country joins a strong bloc and backs its decisions in exchange for protection.

simple: Should your country influence neighboring governments when that makes it safer?

example.agree: Your country backs a candidate next door who promises to fight trafficking at the border.
example.disagree: Your country stays out of neighbors' politics, even if that leaves it less safe.

simple: Should each nation solve its own problems, without other countries getting involved?

example.agree: A country in crisis sorts it out alone, without orders or troops from abroad.
example.disagree: Other countries help resolve the crisis, even if the local government doesn't ask.

simple: Should your country use even military force to protect its interests in its region?

example.agree: A neighbor threatens a power plant that supplies your country, and it sends troops to protect it.
example.disagree: Your country defends its interests in the region only through diplomacy and trade.

simple: Should your country avoid economic penalties on countries just because it disapproves of their governments?

example.agree: Your country keeps trading with a country, even though it disagrees with its government.
example.disagree: Your country cuts trade with a government that violates human rights.

simple: Should no international agreement count for more than the national interest?

example.agree: Your country leaves an international agreement once it starts to hurt the country.
example.disagree: Your country honors what it signed, even when that's costly.

simple: Should your country stay neutral in wars, even when allies ask for support?

example.agree: Two countries go to war, and your country backs neither side, even under pressure.
example.disagree: Your country backs its ally's side, as agreed.

simple: Should what your country does abroad be guided mainly by its own interests?

example.agree: The country picks partners based on what they bring to the national economy.
example.disagree: The country also weighs human rights and the world's good, even at a cost to itself.

simple: Should your country avoid having military bases in other countries?

example.agree: Your country keeps all its soldiers within its own territory.
example.disagree: Your country keeps a base in an allied country to respond quickly to threats.

simple: Should your country pressure neighboring governments that threaten its citizens?

example.agree: Citizens are unjustly jailed next door, and your country threatens to cut deals.
example.disagree: Your country helps the detainees through its consulate, without pressuring the neighbor's government.

simple: Would you support a radical upheaval to take economic power out of the hands of a rich few?

example.agree: Workers take over the big factories and start sharing the profits among everyone.
example.disagree: Wealth shifts gradually, through laws and the market, without upheaval.

simple: Should public services, like buses and trash collection, be run by private companies when there's competition?

example.agree: Three companies bid for the city's trash collection, and the cheapest, most efficient one wins.
example.disagree: The city itself collects the trash, with public employees.

simple: Should companies that matter a lot to the country, like energy or oil companies, stay in government hands?

example.agree: The energy company belongs to the government, which can keep electricity bills low even when that loses money.
example.disagree: The energy company is sold to private owners, who have to compete and be efficient to make a profit.

simple: Should healthcare run mainly through private hospitals and insurance?

example.agree: Most people have health insurance, and the government helps only those who can't pay.
example.disagree: Public hospitals treat everyone for free, as the main system.

simple: Should large companies belong to their workers rather than private owners?

example.agree: A factory's workers own it, vote on decisions, and share the profits.
example.disagree: The factory has owners who invested in it and hire the staff.

simple: Should private companies be allowed to run roads and prisons?

example.agree: A company runs a highway, charges tolls, and keeps the road in good shape.
example.disagree: The government runs roads and prisons directly.

simple: When a service is too expensive for the poor, should the government take it over and provide it?

example.agree: Internet is too pricey in a poor neighborhood, so the government installs public internet there.
example.disagree: The government gives families an allowance to pay the private company.

simple: Should what parents leave their children be protected from taxes that spread wealth around?

example.agree: A family inherits the parents' house and business while paying almost no tax.
example.disagree: Large inheritances pay a high tax, which helps fund public services.

simple: Should healthcare, schools, and water run without the goal of making a profit?

example.agree: Water is supplied by the government at cost, with no one making money from it.
example.disagree: A company supplies the water and profits, as long as it meets quality and price rules.

simple: Should paying taxes be each person's choice?

example.agree: Each person decides whether and how much to contribute to the services they want to support.
example.disagree: Everyone pays mandatory taxes to keep schools, hospitals, and police running.

simple: Should the government guarantee a minimum amount of money every month to people in need?

example.agree: Someone with no income gets a monthly sum from the government for food and bills.
example.disagree: The government helps with training and jobs, but not with a fixed monthly payment.

simple: Should public employees lose the guarantee that they can't be fired?

example.agree: A public employee who performs badly can be fired, like at any company.
example.disagree: Public employees have job security so they can't be fired under political pressure.

simple: Should the government limit the power of very large companies?

example.agree: The government stops a giant company from buying up all its competitors.
example.disagree: A company grows as big as it can, as long as it wins customers fairly.

simple: Should government cash assistance have a time limit?

example.agree: A family gets the aid for up to two years while looking for work.
example.disagree: A family gets the aid for as long as it still needs it, with no deadline.

simple: Should your country break up large estates and give the land to families who have none?

example.agree: A huge, little-used estate is divided among landless families who start farming it.
example.disagree: The estate stays with its owner, and the government helps families buy land another way.

simple: Should each worker negotiate their own pay with the employer, without a union?

example.agree: An employee talks to the company alone and agrees on their pay.
example.disagree: The union negotiates raises for all employees at once.

simple: Should government-owned banks keep lending money for the country's projects and businesses?

example.agree: A public bank lends at low interest to build a railway.
example.disagree: Projects raise money from private banks, and the government doesn't lend.

simple: Should private property be respected even if it leaves the country very unequal?

example.agree: Someone builds up many properties, and the government can't take any of them.
example.disagree: The government can tax more or use some of the property to reduce inequality.

simple: Should government-owned companies stay public, even when they could be sold for a good price?

example.agree: The government gets a great offer for the postal company but decides to keep it.
example.disagree: The government sells the company and uses the money to pay debt or invest.

simple: Should private companies get priority in running public services?

example.agree: A private company takes over running a public hospital and is held to performance targets.
example.disagree: The government runs the hospital itself with its own staff.

simple: Should the government plan key sectors like energy, housing, and industry?

example.agree: The government decides where to build power plants and how many homes to build over the next ten years.
example.disagree: Companies decide where to invest, based on what people buy.

simple: Should prices and wages be set by the market, without government interference?

example.agree: The price of bread and the baker's wages go up or down with demand.
example.disagree: The government controls some prices and sets rules for wages.

simple: There's an agency that decides whether borrowing money gets cheaper or more expensive. Should the president be able to give it orders?

example.agree: Before an election, the government asks for lower interest rates so people buy more, and the central bank goes along.
example.disagree: The central bank keeps interest rates high to slow rising prices, even though the government is asking for the opposite.

simple: Should companies set the terms of employment with minimal government interference?

example.agree: Employer and employee agree on hours and vacation in whatever way suits them both.
example.disagree: The law guarantees maximum hours, vacation, and other rights for everyone.

simple: Should the very rich pay more taxes to fund government programs?

example.agree: People with huge fortunes pay an extra tax that funds schools and hospitals.
example.disagree: Everyone pays the same share, so as not to discourage investors.

simple: Should the government cut taxes so the economy grows?

example.agree: With lower taxes, a company hires more people and opens new stores.
example.disagree: Taxes stay where they are to keep public services running.

simple: Should the government financially support the country's most important industries?

example.agree: The government covers part of an aircraft factory's costs so it doesn't shut down.
example.disagree: Each company supports itself, without government help.

simple: Is keeping jobs more important than raising the minimum wage?

example.agree: The minimum wage rises a little so small shops don't have to lay people off.
example.disagree: The minimum wage rises a lot, even if some businesses hire fewer people.

simple: In a serious crisis, should the government be able to block rent increases?

example.agree: During the crisis, no landlord can raise the rent.
example.disagree: Rents follow the market, and the government helps those who can't pay.

simple: Should the government avoid freezing prices, even when everything is getting very expensive?

example.agree: Even with prices rising fast, the government fights it without banning increases.
example.disagree: The government bans price increases on rice and beans for a few months.

simple: Should the government pick some big domestic companies and help them grow?

example.agree: The government gives cheap loans to a domestic company so it can compete globally.
example.disagree: The government doesn't pick favorites; all companies compete on equal terms.

simple: Should digital currencies like Bitcoin be able to compete freely with government money?

example.agree: A shop accepts Bitcoin, and the customer chooses which money to pay with.
example.disagree: Only official money can be used for payments, and the rest is restricted.

simple: Do you prefer a government-planned economy to letting the market decide?

example.agree: The government decides how many cars and how much food to produce, and at what price.
example.disagree: Companies and consumers decide what to produce and buy.

simple: Should the government avoid adding new rules for businesses?

example.agree: Starting a business takes little paperwork and hardly any licenses.
example.disagree: The government adds rules to protect consumers and the environment.

simple: When the economy is doing badly, should the government spend more to revive it, even by borrowing?

example.agree: In a downturn, the government borrows to build projects and create jobs.
example.disagree: In a downturn, the government cuts spending so as not to add to the debt.

simple: Should the central bank set interest rates without needing government approval?

example.agree: The central bank raises rates to hold prices down, even though the government objects.
example.disagree: The elected government has the final say on interest rates.

simple: Should the government be able to control what our currency is worth against the dollar?

example.agree: The government props up the currency so import prices don't shoot up.
example.disagree: The currency's value moves freely with buying and selling on the market.

simple: Should the central bank be abolished, leaving money and interest rates to the market?

example.agree: Banks and people decide on their own which money to use and what interest to charge.
example.disagree: A central bank manages the currency to prevent crises and runaway prices.

simple: Do you prefer a legal minimum wage to letting every wage be freely negotiated?

example.agree: No company can pay less than the minimum the government sets.
example.disagree: Employer and worker agree on any wage they both accept.

simple: Should people be able to send their money abroad without asking permission?

example.agree: You move your savings to an account in another country with one click.
example.disagree: Large transfers abroad need approval, to prevent money fleeing in a crisis.

simple: Should the government charge a fee on products from abroad so that products made at home sell more?

example.agree: A fee makes imported sneakers more expensive, so the local sneaker factory sells more and keeps its jobs.
example.disagree: Without the fee, imported sneakers stay cheaper for shoppers, even if the local factory has to adapt.

simple: Should taxes on foreign products be nearly scrapped, even if some local factories close?

example.agree: An imported phone gets much cheaper, even if a local factory shuts down.
example.disagree: The tax stays to keep the local factory and its jobs.

simple: Do you prefer limiting imports to protect factory jobs, even if prices go up?

example.agree: The country buys fewer imported clothes, and local factories keep their jobs.
example.disagree: Imported clothes come in freely and are cheaper for everyone.

simple: Should your country make deals to trade with other countries without extra taxes?

example.agree: The country signs a deal, and its fruit starts selling tax-free abroad.
example.disagree: The country keeps its tariffs to control what comes in and goes out.

simple: Should your country make at home everything it uses, even if it costs much more?

example.agree: The country makes its own medicines and computers, even at twice the cost.
example.disagree: The country buys abroad whatever is cheaper and focuses on what it does best.

simple: Should foreign products enter the country with few barriers?

example.agree: An imported product reaches the shop with almost no fees or red tape.
example.disagree: Imported products pay fees and face limits to protect local production.

simple: Should the government limit imports that threaten local factories and jobs?

example.agree: Very cheap imported steel starts ruining local mills, so the government limits it.
example.disagree: The cheap steel comes in, and local businesses that use steel save money.

simple: Should the whole world be one market, with no borders for trade?

example.agree: A company sells to any country as if it were selling to the next town.
example.disagree: Each country keeps its own rules and taxes on what comes in and goes out.

simple: Should foreign companies be barred from buying your country's most important companies?

example.agree: A foreign firm tries to buy the country's biggest energy company, and the government blocks it.
example.disagree: The sale goes through, because the buyer offers the best price and more investment.

simple: Should your country trade more and more with other countries?

example.agree: The country opens new markets and sells meat and planes to dozens of countries.
example.disagree: The country focuses on producing and selling at home.

simple: Should food grown at home take priority over cheaper imported food?

example.agree: The government protects local farmers, even though imported rice is cheaper.
example.disagree: The country buys the cheapest rice, wherever it comes from.

simple: Should it be easier for foreigners to invest in businesses in your country?

example.agree: A foreign company opens a factory with little red tape and creates jobs.
example.disagree: The government sets limits so foreigners don't control key sectors.

simple: When the government buys something, should it favor domestic companies?

example.agree: The government buys uniforms from a domestic factory, even though a foreign one charges less.
example.disagree: The government buys from whoever offers the best price, domestic or foreign.

simple: Should the country trade more with others, even if it comes to depend on them more?

example.agree: The country buys parts abroad and production gets cheaper, though it relies on suppliers.
example.disagree: The country makes parts at home so it isn't at others' mercy.

simple: Should cheap imported electric cars pay an extra tax to protect local factories?

example.agree: A tax makes the imported car pricier, and local carmakers keep their jobs.
example.disagree: The imported electric car arrives cheap, and more people can afford one.

simple: Should taxes on imports be cut, even if the government collects less money?

example.agree: The government lowers import tariffs, and electronics get cheaper.
example.disagree: Tariffs stay, because the government needs that money for public services.

simple: Should production of essentials, like medicines and chips, be protected from foreign competition?

example.agree: The government backs local medicine factories so nothing runs short in a global crisis.
example.disagree: The country buys medicines and chips from whoever makes them best and cheapest worldwide.

simple: Should big foreign companies be able to operate here, even when competing with local firms?

example.agree: A foreign supermarket chain opens stores and lowers prices, even though local shops suffer.
example.disagree: The government limits foreign companies so local businesses survive.

simple: Is depending little on other countries more important than low supermarket prices?

example.agree: The country produces its own food and fuel, even if it costs more.
example.disagree: The country imports whatever is cheapest, and monthly groceries cost less.

simple: Should the world become ever more connected through trade between countries?

example.agree: Parts of a single product are made in ten countries, and everything gets cheaper.
example.disagree: Each country keeps more production at home so it relies less on others.

simple: Should religion stay in each person's private life, without shaping government decisions?

example.agree: A religious politician votes on laws based on evidence and everyone's interests, not on faith.
example.disagree: A politician uses the values of their religion to decide how to vote.

simple: Should your faith guide what you think is right and whom you vote for?

example.agree: Before voting, you think about what your religion teaches on the issue.
example.disagree: You decide your vote without taking religion into account.

simple: Should laws apply equally to everyone, without following the rules of any religion?

example.agree: Whether shops open on Sundays is decided by the economy and the workers, not by one religion's holy day.
example.disagree: Shops close on the holy day of the majority religion, because it is part of the local culture.

simple: Should the country's laws follow the values of the religion most people follow?

example.agree: A family law is written according to what the majority religion teaches.
example.disagree: The law is written to apply equally to people of any religion or none.

simple: Should churches and temples pay taxes like any other organization?

example.agree: A large church pays tax on the money it takes in, like a business.
example.disagree: Churches pay no taxes, because they do social and spiritual work.

simple: Should community life encourage people to practice a religion?

example.agree: The neighborhood holds religious festivals and invites everyone to take part.
example.disagree: The community holds events with no link to religion, so everyone feels welcome.

simple: Should schools, courts, and other public buildings be free of crosses and other religious symbols?

example.agree: The courtroom has no religious objects on the wall.
example.disagree: A cross hangs on the courtroom wall as part of the country's tradition.

simple: Should the country officially declare a religion as its own?

example.agree: The constitution states that the country has an official religion.
example.disagree: The country has no official religion and treats all of them equally.

simple: Should government decisions not be based on religious beliefs?

example.agree: A health law is decided by doctors and research, not religious teachings.
example.disagree: Religious teachings help the government decide what's right.

simple: Should religious traditions be passed on to future generations?

example.agree: Grandparents teach their grandchildren the family's prayers and religious holidays.
example.disagree: Each child grows up and decides alone whether to follow a religion.

simple: Do you prefer a society without religion to a religious one?

example.agree: Almost no one attends places of worship, and people seek answers in science and philosophy.
example.disagree: Most people have faith and belong to a religious community.

simple: Should society make more room for faith?

example.agree: Schools and public events make room for prayers and religious celebrations.
example.disagree: Faith stays in private life and places of worship, out of public spaces.

simple: Should religious holidays stop being national public holidays?

example.agree: A saint's day is no longer a holiday, and those who want to celebrate take a day off.
example.disagree: Important religious dates stay holidays for the whole country.

simple: Should marriage be seen as a religious institution?

example.agree: Marriage is understood as a union blessed by God, celebrated in church.
example.disagree: Marriage is a civil contract, and each couple decides whether they want a religious ceremony.

simple: Should the word "God" be left out of the constitution?

example.agree: The country's highest law doesn't mention God, to include people with no religion.
example.disagree: The constitution mentions God as part of the people's history and faith.

simple: Do you prefer to find your life's meaning in religious faith?

example.agree: In hard times, you look for answers in prayer and your religion.
example.disagree: You find meaning in family, friends, work, or science, without religion.

simple: Should religion not be part of young children's education?

example.agree: Children learn about religions only when they're older and able to choose.
example.disagree: Parents teach their faith to their children from an early age.

simple: If a law goes against your faith, should you follow your faith instead of the law?

example.agree: A doctor refuses a procedure their religion forbids, even though the law requires it.
example.disagree: The doctor follows the law and keeps their faith for personal life.

simple: Should society's rules of right and wrong rest on ideas that don't depend on believing in God?

example.agree: Stealing is wrong because it harms others, and that holds for believers and nonbelievers alike.
example.disagree: Stealing is wrong because it's one of God's commandments.

simple: Should the government protect religious faith as part of the national identity?

example.agree: The government funds the restoration of historic churches and supports traditional religious festivals.
example.disagree: The government treats faith as a private matter and doesn't support it with public money.

simple: Should same-sex couples be able to adopt children with the same rights as other couples?

example.agree: Two married men go through the same adoption process as any couple and adopt a child.
example.disagree: The law gives preference to couples made up of a man and a woman in adoption.

simple: Should the family of a father, a mother, and children be the model for society?

example.agree: Government campaigns present the traditional family as the model to follow.
example.disagree: The government treats all kinds of families as equally valid.

simple: If someone says they're a man or a woman, should that be respected even if they were born with another sex?

example.agree: A trans woman changes her name on her documents and is treated as a woman.
example.disagree: Documents and how people are addressed follow the sex recorded at birth.

simple: Do you prefer society's customs to change slowly rather than quickly?

example.agree: A social change is debated for years before it becomes law.
example.disagree: A social change becomes law as soon as most people support it.

simple: Should universities set aside some places for students from certain racial groups?

example.agree: Some of a program's places are reserved for Black and Indigenous students, who compete among themselves for them.
example.disagree: Every place is decided only by exam score, without considering the applicant's race.

simple: Should marriage be allowed only between a man and a woman?

example.agree: The law recognizes as marriage only the union of a man and a woman.
example.disagree: Two men or two women can also get legally married.

simple: Should gay and lesbian couples be able to show affection in public like any couple?

example.agree: Two women hold hands at the mall, like any other couple.
example.disagree: Same-sex couples avoid showing affection in public places.

simple: Are you against reserving public-sector jobs for people from certain racial groups?

example.agree: Every public-sector job is decided only by test score.
example.disagree: Some of the jobs are reserved for Black candidates, who compete among themselves for them.

simple: Do you think ending a pregnancy in its first weeks is morally acceptable?

example.agree: A woman decides to end a pregnancy in its first weeks, and you see that as a legitimate choice.
example.disagree: You see the pregnancy as a life that should be protected from the start.

simple: Do you think ending a pregnancy is morally wrong?

example.agree: You believe life begins at conception and should be protected from then on.
example.disagree: You believe the decision belongs to the woman, especially early in the pregnancy.

simple: Should teenagers learn about gender identity at school?

example.agree: A class explains what it means to be transgender and talks about respect.
example.disagree: The topic is left to families, and schools don't cover it.

simple: Should children's sex education follow the family's values rather than the school's?

example.agree: Parents decide what their children learn about sex, and when.
example.disagree: The school teaches a standard program on the body and health to every child.

simple: Should offering sex for money be recognized as legitimate work?

example.agree: People doing this work pay taxes, have labor rights, and are protected by law.
example.disagree: The activity isn't recognized as work, and the government tries to reduce it.

simple: Should society avoid adopting gender-neutral language?

example.agree: Schools and government use the traditional forms of the language.
example.disagree: Some documents and schools use neutral forms to include everyone.

simple: Should we eat less meat out of respect for animals?

example.agree: A family starts having meat-free days out of concern for animal suffering.
example.disagree: Eating meat is natural, and the family eats as much as it wants.

simple: Do you think consuming pornography is morally wrong?

example.agree: You believe pornography harms people and relationships.
example.disagree: You see it as each adult's private choice.

simple: Should open relationships and polyamory be as respected as marriage?

example.agree: Three adults live together in a relationship they all agreed on, and are respected as a family.
example.disagree: Marriage between two people remains the model society values.

simple: Should caring for the family be the top priority in a woman's life?

example.agree: A woman puts her career second to look after her children and home.
example.disagree: A woman freely chooses her own priorities, like any man.

simple: Should nudity in films, art, and on beaches not be considered offensive?

example.agree: A beach allows nudity, and a museum displays nude statues without controversy.
example.disagree: Nude scenes are restricted, and the beach requires swimwear.

simple: Should parents have the final say over what their children learn about right and wrong?

example.agree: Parents can pull their child out of a school class that goes against the family's values.
example.disagree: The school teaches values shared by all, even if some parents disagree.

simple: Should society put new technology and more industry first?

example.agree: The country invests heavily in factories and technology research centers.
example.disagree: The country prefers to grow slowly to protect nature and traditional ways of life.

simple: Do you prefer a simple, natural life to one full of technology?

example.agree: You grow some of your own food and use your phone as little as possible.
example.disagree: You make the most of apps, online shopping, and smart devices at home.

simple: Should we use more robots and AI, even if many jobs disappear?

example.agree: Supermarket cashiers are replaced by machines, and prices fall.
example.disagree: The government limits automation to protect jobs.

simple: Should technologies that change the body, the mind, or how people have children be restricted?

example.agree: The law bans choosing a baby's traits in a lab.
example.disagree: Each person decides which technologies to use on their own body.

simple: Should scientists keep creating plants with lab-modified DNA for farming?

example.agree: A modified corn resists a pest, and the farmer loses less of the harvest.
example.disagree: The farmer plants only traditional seeds, even if pests take part of the harvest.

simple: Should we use fewer chemicals on crops, even if harvests shrink?

example.agree: A farmer cuts back on pesticides and harvests less, but with less harm to nature.
example.disagree: The farmer uses approved products to harvest as much as possible and keep food cheap.

simple: Should mining be allowed in protected forests, even if it causes some harm to nature?

example.agree: A mine opens in a protected forest and brings jobs and money to the region.
example.disagree: The forest stays untouched, even with gold and iron beneath it.

simple: Do you prefer preserved nature to rapid industrial growth?

example.agree: A forest is protected, even if a factory won't be built there.
example.disagree: The factory is built and creates jobs, even if part of the forest is cleared.

simple: Should changing people's DNA be allowed to prevent disease?

example.agree: Doctors fix the gene for a serious disease before a baby is born.
example.disagree: The law bans altering human DNA, even to prevent disease.

simple: To fight global warming, is the most important thing to consume less?

example.agree: People buy less, fly less, and reuse what they have.
example.disagree: People keep consuming, and new clean technologies solve the problem.

simple: Should humanity spend money exploring other planets?

example.agree: Countries fund missions to send people to Mars.
example.disagree: Money for space missions goes to solving problems here on Earth.

simple: Should mining in protected forests be banned, even with low-impact technology?

example.agree: A company promises a low-impact mine, but the law doesn't allow it.
example.disagree: The low-impact mine is approved, under strict oversight.

simple: Do you prefer living in a big city to living in the countryside?

example.agree: You like having the subway, hospitals, and lots of job options nearby.
example.disagree: You prefer the calm, space, and closeness to nature of the countryside.

simple: Should altering embryos' DNA to make people smarter be banned?

example.agree: The law bans clinics from creating "enhanced" babies in the lab.
example.disagree: Parents can use the technique, if it's safe, to give their children better chances.

simple: Should healthy people be allowed to get brain devices to think or remember better?

example.agree: Someone gets an implant and can access online information with their thoughts.
example.disagree: Brain implants are limited to treating illness.

simple: Should protecting the environment on Earth come before spending on space travel?

example.agree: Money for a rocket is used to replant forests.
example.disagree: The country invests in space, because it also brings technologies useful on Earth.

simple: Should lab-grown meat replace some livestock farming?

example.agree: Some of the meat at the supermarket is grown in a lab, without slaughtering animals.
example.disagree: Meat keeps coming from traditional animal farming.

simple: Do you prefer a simple life in the countryside to living in a big city?

example.agree: You live in a small country town, close to nature and your neighbors.
example.disagree: You live in a big city, with more services, jobs, and excitement.

simple: To fight global warming, are new technologies better than consuming less?

example.agree: Electric cars and solar power solve the problem without changing people's lives much.
example.disagree: People need to consume and travel less, because technology alone isn't enough.

simple: Are you against artificial implants that make healthy people stronger or faster?

example.agree: A healthy athlete can't swap their legs for faster prosthetics.
example.disagree: A healthy person can get an implant to see in the dark, if they want.
